Subject: Orion RFP — performance section (Q&A)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Attached is Section B of our RFP focused on runtime characteristics and expected scaling behavior. A few clarifying questions from our infra and SRE teams: 

1) For a 2k token average sequence with 64-token prompt prefix, what P50/P95 latency should we expect at steady state on your hosted offering?
2) How does throughput scale with concurrent connections vs concurrency per connection?
3) What warm-up traffic do you observe before KV/prefix caching achieves steady-state benefits?
4) Can you provide a reproducible harness (requests pattern & payloads) we can run against a Dedicated deployment or as an on-site validation?

We also need an attachment referencing a sample CSV you mentioned for raw metrics. Please send the methodology and any assumptions (model variants, quantization, batching) so our procurement and SRE can sign off.

Best,
Elena
Dr. Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Infrastructure, Orion Technologies

Date: Fri, 2025-08-09 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orion RFP — performance section (Q&A)

Elena — thanks, we reviewed Section B. Looping in Dev (solutions) and Lauren (product) to align on a short, reproducible test plan and deliverables. High level answers up front: 

- Hosted (standard production pool) observed P50 ~ 45–70 ms and P95 ~ 180–260 ms for 2k-token average generation when using our medium-latency profile and 8-token generation bursts; numbers vary with requested top_k/top_p samples and streaming vs non-streaming.
- Throughput scales primarily with concurrent request count rather than single-connection concurrency; continuous batching is most effective when many small concurrent requests are present.
- KV/prefix cache benefit typically appears after a small warm-up window (150–500 requests for repetitive prefixes) depending on roster reuse; cold-starts can be mitigated with pre-warm traffic or pinned cache snapshots on Dedicated.

We'll attach a step-by-step harness, a CSV template for raw latencies, and a recommended set of payloads. Can you confirm whether you want us to run the harness in your Dedicated evaluation cluster, or would Orion prefer to run the suite yourselves?

I'll schedule a 30-minute technical run-through; you should see an invite shortly.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Orion RFP — performance section (Q&A) — proposed test harness

Team — drafting the technical response and harness. Key assumptions and test steps (for the attached spreadsheet):

Test environment assumptions:
- Model: open-llama-13b-8bit (quantized) and reference fp16 variant for parity checks
- Hardware for Dedicated validation: 2x A100-80GB (NVLink enabled) or equivalent dedicated pool
- Network: private VPC with <1 ms intra-region RTT; test client colocated in same region where possible

Measurement definitions:
- Latency (per request): measure server-side end-to-end from request receive to final token ACK. Report P10/P50/P90/P95/P99 and mean.
- Throughput: tokens/sec emitted by the runtime aggregated across all worker instances.
- CPU/GPU utilization: sample at 5s intervals during run.
- Token quality checks: deterministic sampling seeds and top_k alignment for reproducibility.

Stepwise harness (short):
1) Warm-up phase: 1000 linear ramp requests over 10 minutes (vary prefixes).
2) Steady-state bursts: 30-minute window at target concurrency levels [10, 50, 100, 250] concurrent requests. Each request asks for 2k tokens generation with a 64-token prompt.
3) Saturation sweep: increase concurrency in steps until throughput flattens; record per-step P95 latencies and GPU utilization.
4) Resilience test: simulate 10% packet loss and a model fallback scenario to validate graceful degradation.

Artifacts we will provide: raw latency CSV, tokens/sec time series, GPU utilization logs, and a short readme with upload instructions. Planning to attach redwood_performance_summary_v2.xlsx.

Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — adding a few customer-facing clarifications and assumptions so procurement and SRE have an apples-to-apples view:

- Metrics reported include server-side processing only; client network variability is excluded unless you request an end-to-end (egress to client) run.
- We will provide both streaming and non-streaming numbers; streaming reduces observed tail latency for interactive token-by-token use cases but can increase backend throughput variability.
- For Dedicated validation we recommend pinning model version v2025-07-llama-q8 (we will provide MD5 and container image tag) to avoid version drift during the test.
- If Orion needs deterministic reruns, we supply a seed and identical request files; note that sampling parameters (top_p/top_k/temperature) materially affect throughput/latency and must be fixed for parity.

Attached: redwood_performance_summary_v2.xlsx and the harness readme in the shared Drive link. We also propose a live run on Wednesday to show the saturation sweep.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
